JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 27.11.2024 at about 06.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing No. KA-41-ER-5594 on Nice road and when he reached Opp. Karnataka Bank, Kodigehalli, Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, Bangalore City, at that time the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-9391 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Kenganar Hospital, Bangalore wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to True life Speciality Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 5 days.

So far the petitioner has spent Rs.3,50,000/-
towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
2(a). Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was working as JCB Cleaner and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In response to the issuance of notice, the Respondents did not appear, hence they were placed ex- parte.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following points arise for the consideration of the court:
POINTS 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a motor vehicle accident on 27.11.2024 at about 6.15 p.m., on Nice road, Opp. Karnataka Bank, Kodigehalli,
Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, Bangalore City and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-9391 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount, if so what is the quantum?
From whom?

2 3. What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
The respondents neither have chosen to conduct the cross examination of Pw.1 nor led their evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials.
7.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Point No.1: Partly in the Affirmative Point No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 27.11.2024 at about 06.15 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing No.
KA-41-ER-5594 on Nice road and when he reached Opp. Karnataka Bank, Kodigehalli,
Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, Bangalore City, at that time the driver of Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-9391(hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
9.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle , the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, wound certificate, notice U/Sec.133 of MVAct and reply thereon, IMV report, charge sheet etc.
10.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Anand/petitioner, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No 366/2024 of Tavarekere Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a) of BNS 2003.

The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281, 125(b) of BNS 2023 and U/sec.146, and 196 of M.V. Act.
11.

At the cost of repetition, at the time of accident the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle from Kodigehalli towards Sulikere and when he reached near Adhishwara Industries the offending vehicle came from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner.
It is true that respondents have not contested the case and there by have not denied the case of the petitioner.
But, the mere fact that the respondents have not contested the case the court cannot with closed eyes accept what ever the contention taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner has relied upon the spot mahazar to prove the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

If the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of the accident is Anand vs M M K Traders on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198413481/
3 nearly 20 feet.

sentences.text: The accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road.
Offending vehicle is a heavy vehicle and the vehicle of the petitioner is a light vehicle.
The petitioner ought to have ride his vehicle on the left side of Kodigehalli road.
But, the petitioner has driven his vehicle in the middle of the road.
The petitioner intentionally has not produced rough sketch to suppress the fact of negligence contributed by him.
Hence, even though charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle, but from the admitted spot mahazar it can be gathered that even petitioner too has contributed negligence.
The negligence contributed by the petitioner and the driver of the offending vehicle is at the ratio of 50:50.
Hence, the petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 50%.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
12. Point No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P3 and 7.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner admitted as an inpatient from 27.11.2024 to 01.12.2024 at True Life Specialty Hospital for a period of 5 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.
13. Dr. Ramesh B., Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him out patient record and x-ray film are got marked as Ex.P11 and Ex.
P12. PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 18.11.2025 for disability assessment.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 30% and on whole body disability at 15%.
14. If the medical records are perused, PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
Further as per the own evidence of PW2.
the petitioner has sustained 30% disability on right lower limb.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb.

sentences.text:
Hence by considering the evidence of the Pw2 so also nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment etc would consider the permanent disability to the whole body at 10%.
15.
Taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
16. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
17. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 15 medical bills for Rs.1,16,767/- as per Ex.P.9.
The respondent has not cross examined the PW.1.
Under such circumstances there is no reason to disbelieve the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
Hence petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,16,767/- under the head medical expenses.

sentences.text: It is stated that petitioner was 35 years and he was working as JCB Cleaner work and thereby earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
To substantiate the said contention the petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
19.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injury and taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient at True Life Speciality Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.49,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
20. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 5 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of money during the year 2024.
21. The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 35 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P10/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1989 that means he was aged about 35 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar Card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 35 years.

22. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.2 even though he has assessed disability on higher side but this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 10% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 35 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16'.
So by applying the multiplier '16' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs./- (i.e., 16,500 x10% x 16 x12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,16,800/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
23. The petitioner at his age of 35 years has suffered two injuries and permanent disability of 10%.
Hence it may cause some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence this court inclines to award sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Heads Amount Rs.
No 1.

Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
2.
Medical expenses Rs.1,16,767/-

3. Towards loss of income during Rs.49,500/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.30,000/-

sentences.text:
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,08,067/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eight Thousand Sixty Seven only).
24.
As per the discussion made above, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the driver of the Goods Carrier have remained absent and have not led any evidence.
Since, the offending vehicle had no insurance policy, the respondent no.1 is liable to pay the compensation.

25. Since both petitioner and respondent no.1 had contributed negligence to an extent of 50:50 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 50%.

The respondent no 1 being the owner is liable to pay 50%
of the awarded compensation to the petitioner.
50% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
In the result Point No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

26. Point No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Point No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
:: ORDER ::
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation Rs.6,08,067/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eight Thousand Sixty Seven only).
The Respondent no.1 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.3,04,034/- at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.3,04,034/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 50% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.3,04,033/-.
